head: 4655e9be45fd0a75e354421c3465ffbbb5537fd7
scope: Body-only independent reading. Gold/teach/hints/reviewer outputs omitted. Approval package issue summaries were previously seen; not a naive blind review.

sentences: When people plan a new project, they tend to imagine the steps going smoothly, one after another.
As a result, their estimates of how long the work will take are usually far too short.
Interestingly, the same people are quite accurate when they estimate how long a similar project will take someone else.
The difference lies in what they pay attention to.
When judging their own plans, they focus on the specific steps in front of them, but when judging others, they recall how such projects have generally turned out.
Thus, the most reliable way to improve a time estimate is to ________.
A writer who checks how long her last three books took, rather than outlining the next one in detail, will rarely be surprised.
body.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: break the project into smaller and clearer steps
ask other people to do part of the work for you
rely on records of comparable work that has already been completed
set a strict deadline before starting the project
focus on the specific obstacles you expect to face

sentences: Many city planners once believed that adding lanes to a crowded road would reduce traffic jams.
At first, the wider roads did seem to move cars faster.
Within a few years, however, the roads were just as crowded as before.
Studies of these cases revealed why: when driving becomes easier, people who used to take the bus, travel at other hours, or stay home begin to drive.
In other words, a new lane does not simply carry the existing traffic; it ________.
This is why some cities now try to manage demand, for example by charging drivers during rush hour, instead of building more roads.
body.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: creates additional traffic that did not exist before
encourages drivers to obey speed limits more carefully
allows buses to travel faster than private cars
reduces the number of people who need to commute
spreads the same number of cars over a wider area

sentences: Museums often place a small label next to each painting, giving its title, date, and a short explanation.
Curators assumed that such labels would deepen visitors' understanding of the art.
Yet when researchers tracked where visitors looked, they found something unexpected.
Visitors who read the label first spent most of their remaining time searching the painting for the details the label had mentioned, and they rarely noticed anything else.
Those who looked at the painting before reading reported more varied observations and remembered the work better a week later.
The researchers concluded that a label read too early can ________.
Some galleries have therefore moved labels a few steps away from the works they describe.
body.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: make visitors lose interest in the museum as a whole
provide historical facts that most visitors already know
help visitors notice details they would otherwise miss
narrow what viewers see to what they have been told
encourage visitors to spend more time at each painting

sentences: Farmers who grow a single crop over large fields can harvest efficiently and sell in bulk.
For decades, this approach was praised as the key to feeding a growing population.
Its weakness becomes clear, however, when a new disease appears.
Because every plant in the field shares the same genes, a pathogen that can infect one plant can infect all of them, and an entire harvest may be lost in a single season.
Fields planted with several varieties rarely suffer such total losses, since some plants are always able to resist.
In this sense, the uniformity that makes a farm efficient is also what ________.
Efficiency, it seems, is measured in good years, while the real test comes in bad ones.
body.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: allows farmers to plant fewer seeds each year
leaves it defenseless against a single threat
makes it popular among large food companies
protects its crops from changes in the weather
forces farmers to grow several varieties at once

sentences: Parents and teachers often praise children by telling them how smart they are.
In one series of experiments, children who were praised for their intelligence after solving easy puzzles were later offered a choice between an easy task and a challenging one.
Most of them chose the easy task, apparently to avoid any risk of looking less clever.
Children who had instead been praised for the effort they put in mostly chose the challenging task and kept trying longer when it became difficult.
The praise had taught each group a different lesson about what success means.
Praise for ability tends to make children ________ challenges, whereas praise for effort encourages them to welcome difficulty.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? (근거 문장은 요약문을 제외한 본문 문장에서 고를 것)
choices: seek out more often
give up halfway through
solve more quickly
hide their mistakes in
steer away from

sentences: Before the invention of cheap clocks, most people had no need to know the exact time.
Work began at sunrise and ended when the light faded or the task was done.
Then factories arrived and changed this pattern.
Because machines needed hundreds of workers to start and stop at the same moment, owners paid wages by the hour rather than by the task and punished lateness of even a few minutes.
Over time, people came to feel that time itself was something that could be spent, saved, or wasted.
Our sense of time as a valuable resource, then, ________.
It is a habit of mind we inherited, not a fact we discovered.
body.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: was first developed by people who worked outdoors
is a natural feeling shared by all human societies
grew out of the demands of industrial work
makes modern workers less productive than before
depends on how accurate our clocks have become

sentences: The Varnel Lantern Festival is held every autumn in the small river town of Ostrey.
It began in 1872, when fishermen floated paper lanterns downstream to thank the river for a safe season.
Today, visitors are invited to make their own lanterns at workshops that open three days before the festival.
Only lanterns made of paper and plant-based glue may be placed on the water, because the town wants to protect the fish.
On the final night, the lanterns are released together at sunset while a local choir sings traditional songs.
Volunteers collect the lanterns at a net downstream the next morning, and the paper is turned into compost for public gardens.
Although the festival is free, donations are used to repair the old wooden bridge where the release takes place.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 어부들이 무사한 조업 철에 감사하는 뜻에서 시작되었다.
축제 사흘 전부터 등 만들기 작업장이 열린다.
물고기 보호를 위해 등을 물에 띄우지 않고 강가에 걸어 둔다.
마지막 날 밤 해 질 녘에 등을 함께 띄워 보낸다.
기부금은 오래된 나무다리 수리에 쓰인다.

sentences: The marsh pika is a small mammal that lives only in the reed beds of the imaginary Tarrow Valley.
Unlike most pikas, which live among rocks on mountains, it builds floating nests out of woven reeds.
Adults weigh about 120 grams and have unusually long back toes that help them swim short distances.
During summer, each family gathers wet grass and dries it on top of the nest to store for winter.
Marsh pikas communicate with soft whistles, and young pikas learn the family's whistle within two weeks of birth.
Because their reed beds are shrinking, the species has been protected by valley law since 1998.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Tarrow 계곡의 갈대밭에서만 산다.
갈대를 엮어 물에 뜨는 둥지를 만든다.
긴 뒷발가락이 짧은 거리를 헤엄치는 데 도움이 된다.
여름에 풀을 모아 둥지 위에서 말려 저장한다.
새끼는 태어난 지 두 달이 지나야 가족의 휘파람을 익힌다.

sentences: Elna Corrow, a fictional clockmaker from the port city of Bresk, is remembered for inventing the tide clock.
As a girl, she repaired ship instruments in her uncle's workshop instead of attending school.
Her tide clock used a second hand that moved with the moon, so sailors could read the time of high water at a glance.
At first, harbor officials refused to use it, saying that printed tide tables were already accurate enough.
After the clock correctly warned of an unusually high tide in 1851, the harbor ordered twelve of them.
Corrow never applied for a patent, and she taught her method freely to any apprentice who asked.
One of her original clocks still runs in the Bresk maritime museum.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 학교에 다니면서 삼촌의 작업장에서 일을 배웠다.
그녀의 시계는 만조 시각을 한눈에 읽을 수 있게 했다.
항만 관리들은 처음에 그 시계의 사용을 거부했다.
특허를 신청하지 않고 방법을 자유롭게 가르쳤다.
그녀가 만든 원래 시계 하나가 지금도 박물관에서 작동한다.

sentences: The Halden Seed Library is a fictional community project that lends seeds instead of books.
Members borrow seeds in spring, grow the plants in their own gardens, and return new seeds in autumn.
Each packet comes with a card on which growers record the soil type and the date of the first flower.
The library focuses on old local vegetable varieties that are no longer sold in shops.
Children under twelve may borrow seeds only when an adult member signs the card with them.
Since the project started, the number of varieties it keeps has grown from 40 to more than 300.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 회원은 봄에 씨앗을 빌리고 가을에 새 씨앗을 돌려준다.
씨앗 봉투의 카드에 토양 종류와 첫 개화 날짜를 기록한다.
상점에서 더 이상 팔지 않는 지역 토종 채소 품종에 집중한다.
12세 미만 어린이는 어른 회원 없이 혼자서도 씨앗을 빌릴 수 있다.
보유 품종 수가 40종에서 300종 이상으로 늘었다.

sentences: The glass frog of the fictional Merrin Islands is known for skin so thin that its heart can be seen beating.
It is active mainly at night and spends the day resting under wide leaves near waterfalls.
Males, not females, guard the eggs, which are laid on leaves that hang over streams.
When the tadpoles hatch, they drop into the water below and grow there for about three months.
The frog's call is so high that most human visitors cannot hear it without special equipment.
Island researchers count the frogs each year, and the population has stayed stable for a decade.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 낮에 주로 활동하고 밤에는 폭포 근처에서 쉰다.
알이 부화하면 올챙이는 아래 물로 떨어져 약 석 달간 자란다.
암컷이 시냇물 위 잎에 낳은 알을 지킨다.
울음소리가 낮아서 방문객 대부분이 쉽게 들을 수 있다.
섬 연구자들은 이 개구리의 수를 따로 세지 않는다.

sentences: The Kestly Night Market is a fictional weekly market held in the parking lot of an old train station.
It opens every Friday from six in the evening until midnight, except in January, when it closes for repairs.
Sellers must use their own lights, and many hang small solar lamps that they charge during the day.
Most stalls sell food, but a corner of the market is reserved for students who sell handmade crafts.
Visitors who bring their own cups and plates receive a small discount at every food stall.
The market was started by a group of bus drivers who wanted a place to eat after late shifts.
It now attracts about two thousand visitors each week.
body.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 1월을 제외하고 매주 금요일 저녁에 열린다.
판매자는 자신의 조명을 직접 사용해야 한다.
학생 공예품 구역은 따로 없고 모든 노점이 음식을 판다.
자기 컵과 접시를 가져오면 할인을 받는다.
늦은 근무 뒤 식사할 곳을 원한 버스 기사들이 시작했다.

sentences: When a new public library opens, its planners usually count success by the number of books borrowed.
Yet some of the busiest libraries lend fewer books each year than they did a decade ago.
Visitors come instead to use quiet rooms, attend free classes, or simply sit somewhere warm without being asked to buy anything.
For many residents, especially the elderly and the unemployed, the library is the only indoor public place that expects nothing from them.
Measuring such a building by its loans is like rating a park by the tickets it sells.
What a library offers its community cannot be found on a checkout record.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 "rating a park by the tickets it sells"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: charging people for a space they once enjoyed for free
using a narrow count that misses what a place truly gives
assuming that popular public spaces need more funding
counting visitors more carefully at the entrance gate
comparing libraries with parks to decide which is better

sentences: Many companies reward employees for meeting a single number, such as calls answered per hour.
At first the number rises quickly, and managers are pleased.
Soon, however, workers learn to end calls early or transfer difficult customers to someone else.
The figure keeps improving while the customers' problems remain unsolved.
In such offices, the scoreboard ends up playing a different game from the one on the field.
A measure that people are paid to raise slowly stops telling managers what they wanted to know.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 "the scoreboard ends up playing a different game from the one on the field"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Workers compete with each other to post the top figures.
Managers lose interest in the figures they once relied on.
Customers and staff judge success by different standards.
Gains on paper conceal service that is getting no better.
Staff enjoy their tasks more once the job becomes a contest.

sentences: Young researchers are often advised to choose a narrow question and stay with it.
The advice has merit, since focus allows depth that scattered interest cannot reach.
But scientists who spend decades inside one small problem sometimes lose the ability to notice what lies just beyond it.
A finding from a neighboring field may answer their question, yet they never read that field's journals.
Such a researcher digs a well so deep that he can no longer see the sky.
The most productive careers, studies suggest, combine long focus with regular visits to unfamiliar areas.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 "digs a well so deep that he can no longer see the sky"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: grows so absorbed that outside help goes unnoticed
works on one problem until his motivation runs out
picks a question too small to yield useful results
switches topics too often to reach any real depth
leans on others' results instead of his own work

sentences: Small towns that lose their only grocery store rarely notice the full cost at once.
Residents simply drive to the next town, and life seems to go on.
Over time, however, the trip becomes a reason to shop, eat, and see a doctor elsewhere as well.
The pharmacy and the café that depended on grocery shoppers begin to close one by one.
The store, it turns out, was not one thread in the town's fabric but the knot that held many threads together.
When planners decide which businesses to support, they should ask what else depends on them.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 "the knot that held many threads together"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: a shop that relied on nearby businesses for its customers
a store that sold enough goods to spare residents a trip
a business that competed with the pharmacy and the café
the shop that brought the most money into the town
a business whose loss drags other local life down too

sentences: In one experiment, volunteers were asked to taste two cups of coffee and say which they preferred.
Unknown to them, both cups were filled from the same pot.
One cup, however, was served in a heavy ceramic mug, the other in a thin paper cup.
Most volunteers described the coffee in the mug as richer and were willing to pay more for it.
When the same test was repeated with the volunteers' eyes covered and the coffee poured into identical glasses, the preference disappeared.
Similar results have appeared with wine served in expensive bottles and food on fine plates.
body.stem: 다음 글을 통해 추론할 수 있는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 도자기 잔은 커피를 더 오래 따뜻하게 해 맛을 좋게 한다.
종이컵 커피를 고른 사람들은 맛에 더 예민한 편이다.
커피 맛을 공정하게 비교하려면 담는 용기를 똑같이 해야 한다.
눈을 가리면 사람들은 커피와 다른 음료도 잘 구별하지 못한다.
비싼 병에 담긴 와인은 실제로도 품질이 더 좋은 경우가 많다.

sentences: A student who rereads a chapter three times often feels well prepared for the test.
Each reading goes more smoothly, and the familiar sentences seem to confirm that the material has been learned.
But recognizing a page is not the same as being able to rebuild its ideas without it.
When the book is closed and a question demands an explanation, that comfortable feeling often vanishes.
Rereading, in this sense, polishes the window without opening it.
Testing oneself, though less pleasant, is what shows whether the knowledge can actually be used.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 "polishes the window without opening it"가 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: slowly lowers the student's interest in the subject
makes the ideas clearer and easier to grasp each time
costs more time than it saves in the days before a test
builds a sense of ease that fails once recall is needed
readies the student to teach the chapter to others

sentences: Students often assume that the hours spent sleeping are simply lost from their study time.
However, the sleeping brain is far from idle.
During deep sleep, it replays the patterns formed during the day and strengthens the connections that support them.
As a result, material reviewed before bed is often remembered better the next morning than material reviewed in the early afternoon.
Students who cut their sleep in order to study longer therefore lose part of the very benefit they are working for.
Every hour they win at the desk is an hour taken from the process that turns study into lasting memory.
Sleep, in short, is not a break from learning but one of its stages.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: Birds that live in cities face a problem their forest relatives rarely meet: constant noise from traffic.
Low-pitched engine sounds can easily drown out a song sung in the usual range.
Many urban birds now sing at a higher pitch, above the range where engine noise is loudest.
Some also shift their singing to the early hours, before the morning rush begins.
These changes are not free, however.
A higher song may travel a shorter distance, and females in some species still prefer the lower notes.
Adapting to the city, then, means trading one disadvantage for another.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: In one common classroom experiment, half the students take notes by hand while the other half type them on laptops.
Afterward, both groups are tested on the content of the lecture.
Typists usually record far more words, often copying the speaker almost exactly.
Hand-writers, by contrast, cannot keep up and must decide what is worth writing down.
That forced selection turns out to be an advantage.
Having to leave things out, rather than holding the students back, actually helps them learn.
To choose what to record, they must process the ideas in their own words, and on questions that ask them to explain concepts, the hand-writers tend to perform better.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: Many neighborhoods now run libraries that lend tools instead of books.
A resident who needs a drill for one afternoon can borrow it rather than buy one that will sit in a drawer for years.
The idea saves money, but its effects reach further.
Fewer tools need to be manufactured, shipped, and eventually thrown away.
In addition, borrowers often meet their neighbors at the counter and trade advice about repairs.
Some libraries even report that members have begun fixing broken items for one another.
What starts as a way to share objects can thus end up building a community.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: In the past century, engineers straightened many winding rivers so that water would drain from farmland more quickly.
This made floods worse in the towns farther downstream.
Water that had once spread slowly across the bends now arrived all at once.
Today, some regions are digging out new curves and reconnecting the wetlands that were drained.
Once this work is finished, the river is left to shape its own course again.
In several places, downstream floods have already become smaller and slower.
This pattern suggests that a river's crooked path was never a flaw that needed correcting.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: Taste seems to be a simple matter of what is on the tongue.
In reality, it is shaped heavily by what we expect before the first bite.
In one kind of study, people drink the same juice from two cups, one labeled as a premium brand and the other as a store brand.
Then they rate each cup, and most report that the premium cup tastes sweeter and richer.
Expectation works almost like an ingredient that we add without noticing.
Food companies understand this effect well.
Consequently, they often spend as much effort on packaging colors and labels as on the recipe itself.
body.stem: 표시된 두 문장 사이의 관계로 알맞은 것을 고르시오.

sentences: Most people assume that memory works like a video recorder.
In reality, each act of recall rebuilds the event from scattered pieces.
The details that a person remembers most clearly about a dramatic day often changes over the years.
This happens because the brain fills gaps with what seems likely.
Researchers who compare early and late accounts find that confidence stays high even when accuracy drops.
Feeling certain, therefore, is not the same as being right.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Cities that plant trees along their streets often report cooler summer temperatures.
Shade lowers the amount of heat absorbed by the pavement during the day.
Leaves also release water vapor, which cools the surrounding air.
Planners have learned that the benefit depends on where the trees are placed.
A row of trees along a busy road can do more than a large park located far from homes.
That residents value most is not the number of trees but the shade on their daily walks.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Students surprising by a low score often decide that they lack talent.
Yet the score usually reflects how they studied rather than what they can do.
Rereading notes feels productive, but it leaves little trace in memory.
Testing oneself, by contrast, forces the mind to retrieve information.
Learners who switch to this method often find their next results encouraging.
The lesson is that a disappointing grade is feedback, not a final judgment.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Good listeners do much more than stay silent while others speak.
They pay attention to tone as well as to words.
When a friend sounds tired, a good listener notices it and adjusts the conversation.
Such listeners lean forward, ask short questions, and repeating key words back to the speaker.
These small actions show that the speaker's message has been received.
People treated this way tend to share more openly the next time.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Among the oldest tools of agriculture is the simple irrigation ditch.
The rivers that wind through the valley and feed its many small farms have shifted its course several times over the past century.
Only after a severe flood did the farmers begin to record the water levels each spring.
These records, kept in a village office for decades, now allow engineers to predict floods.
Rarely does a community's careful habit prove so valuable to people living generations later.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Many old buildings in cities are now being turned into libraries and community centers.
Converting a factory often costs less than constructing a new structure.
In addition, the materials used in the original walls do not need to produce again.
Architects also say that visitors enjoy seeing traces of the building's past.
A brick floor marked by old machines reminds people of the work once done there.
Such reuse lets a city keep its history while meeting new needs.
body.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

sentences: Farmers in dry regions have long searched for crops that can survive with very little rain.
One approach is to plant varieties whose roots reach deep into the soil, where moisture remains after the surface has dried.
In recent trials, such deep-rooted wheat continued to grow through a month without rainfall.
More importantly, it yielded nearly twice as much grain per field as the traditional variety did.
For families who depend on a single harvest, that difference can decide whether they have enough food for the year.
Researchers now hope to combine deep roots with resistance to common plant diseases.
body.stem: 밑줄 친 낱말 'yielded'의 이 글에서의 뜻으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 굴복했다
양보했다
산출했다
흡수했다
손실을 냈다

sentences: Before a new bridge is opened to traffic, engineers must show that its design is safe.
They test models in wind tunnels, measure how the steel behaves under heavy loads, and check every calculation twice.
Only when the results agree with one another do they declare the structure sound.
Even then, sensors are placed along the bridge to report any unexpected movement in the years that follow.
This combination of careful testing and constant monitoring is why serious bridge failures are now extremely rare.

sentences: Children learn early that some promises are easy to make and hard to keep.
A parent who says "We'll go to the beach tomorrow" and then cancels may think the matter is small.
